outcome: Prevalence of baby-related breastfeeding problems (improper latching, babies sleep while sucking, oral thrush, vomiting after feeding)
Prevalence of mother-related breastfeeding problems (sore nipples, shooting pain during breastfeeding, short or retracted nipples, inadequate milk, engorged breasts, mastitis)
cohort: 300 postpartum mothers from a tertiary care center.
finding: Improper latching due to short nipples was identified as the most common breastfeeding problem, suggesting that education could minimize most feeding difficulties.
birth_weight: 20% of babies (60 babies) were low birth weight
